userStories.title: Make C# benchmark multi-threaded with distributed keys
userStories.description: As a benchmark runner, I need the C# benchmark to use multi-threaded execution and distributed unique keys so it matches the Haskell benchmark methodology.
acceptanceCriteria: Program.cs RunBenchmark() uses Parallel.For or Task.Run with thread count from Environment.ProcessorCount (matching Haskell's getNumCapabilities)
Each thread collects latencies in a thread-local list (no shared contention), merged after completion
Replace single fixed key 'bench:key' with distributed unique keys per iteration using pattern 'bench:set:{i}', 'bench:r:{i}', etc. matching Haskell's mkKey pattern
Pre-populate a 10,000-key read pool ('bench:r:0' through 'bench:r:9999') before read benchmarks, matching Haskell's readKeyPool
DEL benchmark uses unique keys per iteration (not reusing 'bench:delkey')
Throughput computed from wall-clock time: ops_per_sec = totalIterations / wallClockSeconds (not sum of individual latencies)
Warm-up phase runs per-thread at 10% of iterations (matching Haskell)
Benchmark keys cleaned up after all benchmarks complete
Program builds with dotnet build
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Reference Haskell Main.hs for the exact key patterns, iteration counts, and concurrency model. The C# benchmark must produce the same JSON output schema as before (operation -> {p50_us, p95_us, p99_us, ops_per_sec, iterations}).
